headline: Claimed strikes on Riyadh and Yanbu sit against a CENTCOM report of record Hormuz throughput across a fully halted weekend, lifting late-window Stress while Tail stays near its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the final observed futures print was not a session extreme - and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, three hours after the last slot in this window. No published hour contains a tradable tape. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, with the benchmark yield back around 5.00% on 18 September after the 16 September hike. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, a third consecutive decline. The macro backdrop stays two-sided: the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote while stating that inflation remains elevated, the Bank of Japan lifted its own policy rate to 1.25% on Friday - a 31-year high - and gold closed at 4,380.01 with silver at 66.35. The geopolitical file is unchanged in direction but better documented this run. Overnight into 19 September, Houthi forces claimed two operations, one against sensitive sites in Riyadh, where an Aramco fuel depot near King Khalid International Airport burned after air-raid alerts, and one against Aramco facilities at Yanbu, the Red Sea export gateway whose loadings have been suspended since 11 September and whose feeder East-West pipeline, normally 4-5 million barrels a day, remains shut. Saudi authorities have issued no confirmation of damage and did not respond to press enquiries. Running directly against that, CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said in a video message on Saturday that oil and gas transits through the Strait of Hormuz have reached a six-month high, with more than one billion barrels moved out of the Gulf over roughly two months and the main transit lanes clear of mines. Crude had already fallen for three sessions into Friday on easing Saudi supply fears. The weekend is therefore genuinely two-sided, and none of it is priceable inside this window: it must be absorbed in one step at a reopen that sits three hours beyond the final slot. Because the venue is shut throughout, Tail holds its structural floor - there is no mechanism by which mean reversion can fail inside a halted market. Tail eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches a window high of 8 in the final slot, reflecting accumulating untested headline exposure ahead of an unpriced reopen rather than any observed structure. Stress traces the same shape from a low of 22 to a high of 29, crossing into the moderate band from 11:00Z Sunday. Confidence is solid rather than high: the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified, but it is static, and Friday's marks age through every subsequent hour with no tape able to refresh them. The shared Finviz context file was read for this run and reported partial collection, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so cross-asset futures confirmation was unavailable and the assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail opened the window at 16 in Friday's late triple-witching session, fell through 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, and then held 5 across the final twenty slots. Stress began at 44 and decayed through 33, 28, 27 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive hours before edging back to 24 across the last three slots. Dominant mode was trend-up for the single Friday close slot and normal for the remaining 23 hours. Confidence peaked at 88 at the close and then declined steadily to 74 as the live tape gave way to the weekend and Friday's marks aged. No hour in the lookback is unavailable.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, three hours after the final slot here. No published hour contains a tradable tape, and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window - the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, and the first high-impact release is Wednesday's set of S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for one hour, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt from 21:00Z Saturday, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday, steps to 6 from 11:00Z, reaches 7 from 15:00Z and prints a window high of 8 in the final 19:00Z slot as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates toward an unpriced reopen. Stress mirrors that shape between a low of 22 and a high of 29, crossing into the moderate band from 11:00Z Sunday. Confidence declines gently from 73 to 65 as Friday's verified marks age. Every step is a function of venue distance and accumulating unpriced information, not of observed price structure; dominant mode stays normal throughout because a halted venue has no structure to classify. Tail is capped in single digits because the weekend evidence remains genuinely two-sided: claimed strikes on Riyadh and Yanbu argue one way, while CENTCOM's six-month-high Hormuz throughput statement, no Saudi confirmation of damage and three straight sessions of crude decline argue the other.
